ps140: The Spirit of God has been poured forth upon us, the faithful,* as, moved by Him, the honoured Joel said in prophecy;* and he discloses the revelation of divine mysteries and prophesies.* And we who have received His activity* are illumined with divine radiance and with the grace of God.

Full of divine eloquence, the wondrous Joel issues forth from Your house* like a well-spring watering men’s souls, O Master,* and has let fall upon us the sweetness which delights our thoughts,* in that he has been exalted by the Spirit* and elevated by virtue to divine heights.

With your boldness as a prophet and your noetic closeness to God, O Joel,* by which you see heavenly visions,* move Him to pity for us who with faith celebrate your memory, O glorious one,* asking remission of transgressions,* a share in divine delights and great mercy.

Beholding the sufferings of the right victorious martyrs,* full of divine boldness you entered enter the arena, O Varus,* and preached Christ, who became a man for our sake;* and you were not afraid of death or the torments that lay before you.* Wounded and mercilessly dismembered, you rejoiced with perfect understanding, O wise one,* looking toward the glory which abides for those who love God.

Seeing your flesh and blood falling away, O athlete,* you most valiantly endured as though another were suffering in your stead.* Bound to a tree, you endured the laceration of the iniquitous most patiently;* and you committed your spirit into the hands of God,* astonishing those who beheld you with your steadfast opposition.* Wherefore, we honour you, O wise Varus, whose courage was so great,* and who cast down the tyrant with your pangs.

The wondrous Cleopatra, having embalmed you with spices, interred you in the earth,* and raised up to you a holy church, celebrating your feast, O wondrous Varus,* and entreating you with faith.* Her children you enrolled in the noetic army,* adorned with glory and numbered among the choirs of the saints,* whose portion you vouchsafe also to us* who piously celebrate your festival, O right wondrous martyr.
theotokion: Rejoice, O root bedewed!* Rejoice, O staff of Aaron* who budded forth the never-fading* and ever-living Flower,* O pure Maiden,* thou right fruitful garden* who shone forth from the root of Jesse* the Tree of life,* and dost nurture mortals with noetic bread!* Rejoice, O most precious robe of purple,* Bride of God, the King of heaven,* most radiant crown,* adornment of hierarchs!* Rejoice, thou who alone art most pure!
stavrotheotokion: Of old, when the unblemished ewe-lamb, the immaculate Mistress,* beheld her Lamb upon the Tree of the Cross,* she exclaimed maternally and cried out in wonder:* “O my Child most sweet, what new and strange thing is this that I see?* How have the thankless multitude given You over to the tribunal of Pilate* and condemned You, the Life of all, to death?** Yet I hymn Your ineffable condescension, O Word!”
